finding: The live range of $170-$700 is about right, and slightly generous at the top for a single front door. Built totals (parts + stated hours x $120-$160/hr, the national middle labor rate used for these checks): economy 2015 Corolla about $145-$606 (0.5-1.5 hr); midsize 2009 CR-V about $119-$420 (0.5-1.5 hr); truck 2017 F-150 about $230-$390 (1.0-1.5 hr); luxury 2015 BMW 328i about $192-$524 (0.8-1.5 hr). The lowest totals ($119-$145) combine an online aftermarket part with a 0.5-hour manufacturer warranty time, which is less than a shop normally charges for either, so $170 is a fair floor. The highest total we can build is about $606 (genuine Toyota lock assembly at list, $366, plus 1.5 hours); YourMechanic's shop/dealer figure for an Acura TLX tops out near $601 and RepairPal's national average is $381-$484. So $700 is above anything we could build at $160/hr, but it is plausible at a dealer charging more than $160/hr or once diagnosis is added; a ceiling nearer $600-$650 would match the evidence more closely. On these four vehicles the actuator comes as one piece with the door latch, which is why OEM parts run $150-$366 rather than the $30-$60 of a bare actuator motor. How solid the labor times are: only the CR-V has manufacturer-stated times (Honda warranty flat rates of 0.5 hr for the driver's actuator and 0.6 hr for a front passenger latch assembly); the F-150 low end is a parts seller's 'approx 1 hour'; the Corolla low end borrows the Honda time and is not a Toyota figure; the BMW class and every high end rest on one named author's general statement of 0.8-1.5 hours at a dealership. No Toyota, Ford or BMW stated time for replacing one front latch was found (Ford's door latch recalls list times only for all four doors or for water shields), so confidence is low. The CR-V aftermarket price is for a part whose page does not say which door it fits.
extras: A quote often adds a diagnosis fee (a lock that will not work can also be a fuse, switch, wiring in the door hinge area, or a control module, not the actuator), shop supplies, and sales tax. Broken door panel clips, a vapor barrier reseal, or a lock rod or cable are sometimes added. Other doors are quoted separately, and when one actuator has failed from age the others often follow. Some vehicles need the new latch programmed or the door ajar and anti-theft functions checked afterward.
